rendering.persona_description: Mohammed is a 67-year-old retired machinist who transitioned in his mid-fifties after decades of feeling like something was wrong that he couldn't name. He restores old radios in his garage, reads history books, and still argues with his wife Carol about whether the Tigers will ever win another pennant. He has three grown kids from his marriage before transition and four grandchildren he adores, and like any grandfather he sometimes catches himself thinking twice when he's carrying one of them down the stairs.
rendering.clinical_context: Mohammed has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, he has occasional unwanted thoughts, such as a flash of worry about tripping while carrying one of his grandchildren down the stairs, but these pass on their own within moments and he doesn't do anything to check, avoid, or neutralize them. He goes about his days without any lasting distress from these fleeting thoughts.
rendering.behavioral_description: Mohammed talks in short, clipped sentences and gets prickly fast if he feels like he's being managed or lectured, especially about what he 'should' be doing with his time or his health. He'll argue a point just to test whether it holds up, and he softens only when he feels like he's being reasoned with rather than instructed. He's plainly proud of his independence and doesn't like it questioned, but he'll admit when he's wrong if the argument is good enough.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in their own home
traits.communication_register: blunt, dry, occasionally gruff, uses plain working-class language
traits.help_seeking_orientation: not applicable; he has no mental-health condition to seek help for, and is generally skeptical of anyone suggesting he needs fixing
traits.cognitive_style: analytical and detail-oriented, skeptical of anything that sounds like a script

clinical_history.history: No history of mental-health symptoms or treatment; he has gone through life without any such concerns, aside from the everyday, fleeting worries most people experience.
